paper_title: Thermal Simulation of a CPU Based on Model Order Reduction

scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 1 (floorplan and 3D structure of the Alpha EV6) with the setup text on page 2 and results in Figs. 3 and 4 on page 3
scenario.description: Dynamic thermal simulation of the Alpha EV6 CPU. FEniCS finite element DNS (129x129x7 mesh, 3 ms) provides training data for a POD reduced-order model. POD models with 1, 3 and 5 modes are compared with the DNS on the dynamic temperature at functional unit C and on x/y temperature profiles through hot spots A, B and C at t = 3 ms.
scenario.architecture: Alpha EV6 processor, 3D layered chip structure. Floorplan from the HotSpot site, with adiabatic side and top surfaces and a Robin boundary condition at the substrate bottom.
scenario.workload: Uniform power pulses applied in functional units A, B and C. Each has a period of 3.333 us and represents an average over 10k cycles at 3 GHz.
scenario.operating_point: Transient simulation to t = 3 ms. Ambient temperature is 0 C, and temperatures are reported as degrees above ambient. Per-block powers and dimensions are not given numerically in the text.

original_setup.solver: FEniCS finite element direct numerical simulation (129x129x7 mesh, 3 ms transient). It provides training data for a POD-Galerkin reduced-order model built with the method of snapshots.
original_setup.optimizer: None. POD modes come from an eigen-decomposition (Fredholm equation) of the snapshot correlation tensor, not from a design optimizer.
original_setup.controller: None. No thermal management controller or DTM policy is used.
original_setup.benchmark: Alpha EV6 CPU (floorplan from the HotSpot site, Fig. 1). POD models with 1, 3 and 5 modes are compared against the FEniCS DNS on the dynamic temperature at functional unit C and on x/y temperature profiles through hot spots A, B and C at t = 3 ms (Figs. 3 and 4).

thermal_observable.unit: degrees above ambient (ambient = 0 C), i.e. K rise
thermal_observable.location: Device layer hot spot in functional unit C (Fig. 4a); x/y profiles through hot spots A, B and C at t = 3 ms (Figs. 4b, 4c). No numeric value is given in the text.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Time-resolved point temperature at the hot spot over 0-3 ms; spatial line profiles at t = 3 ms; POD models with 1, 3 and 5 modes compared against the FEniCS DNS.

physical_mismatches.reason: The original scenario is a 3D layered chip (129x129x7 mesh) with a device layer and substrate. A 2D or single-layer model cannot reproduce the vertical conduction and substrate Robin cooling path.
The original is a transient simulation (3 ms) with pulsed power (3.333 us period, averaged over 10k cycles at 3 GHz). A steady-state model would not match the reported dynamic temperature at unit C.

The original solver is a FEniCS FEM DNS and a POD-Galerkin reduced-order model with a data-driven mode basis. A Studio solver differs in discretization and cannot reproduce the 1/3/5-mode ROM comparison.

The original boundary conditions are adiabatic on the sides and top and Robin at the substrate bottom with 0 C ambient. No package, heat sink, interposer or realistic cooling stack is modeled, and the Robin coefficient is not given.
The paper has no controller, optimizer, reliability analysis or 2.5D/3D integration study. Any Studio controller or optimizer would be an addition outside the original scenario.

missing_inputs: Numeric x_m, y_m, width_m and height_m for every Alpha EV6 block. Fig. 1 only shows the floorplan graphically, and the HotSpot URL (ref 22, page 4) is not a pinned packet asset.
Per-block power_rows in watts for units A, B and C, including pulse amplitude and duty. No numeric powers are published and total power must not be split without a published rule.
Chip lateral dimensions, layer thicknesses (7 mesh layers) and material properties (k, density, specific heat) for the device layer and substrate.
Robin boundary heat transfer coefficient at the substrate bottom.
Numeric temperature values for the hot-spot observable. Figs. 3 and 4 are plots without tabulated values and none were digitized.

FEniCS scripts, mesh, POD mode data and configuration files. The packet contains no assets and no code or data availability statement; the FEniCS and HotSpot URLs are software or tool sites and do not prove the inputs exist.
Studio package and material assumptions were not supplied in the packet, so they cannot be recorded.
No complete experiment (geometry plus same-scenario powers) can be assembled, so no floorplan is returned.
